open_points.subject: ProgressPhoto binary delivery failure
open_points.text: R0-12 says “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error,” while A14 says “A missing source object is an explicit unavailable/not-found failure.”
open_points.question: When an authorized, visible progress photo’s source object is missing, must the response be the explicit storage-unavailable error, or may it be the not-found failure allowed by A14?
options: Always return the explicit storage-unavailable error for a missing photo object.
Return not-found for a missing photo object, reserving storage-unavailable for another storage failure.
Treat unavailable/not-found as one error category whose externally observable response is fixed later.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the newer object-specific R0-12 rule and return the explicit storage-unavailable error.

witness.initial: An active viewer has a valid session and grant for an active project; a client-visible ProgressPhoto record exists, but its file_ref resolves to no stored object.
events: The viewer requests the photo binary by photo_id.
Project access and visibility checks pass.
Binary storage reports that the source object is missing.
outcomes: R0-12 yields an explicit storage-unavailable error.
A14 permits a not-found failure for the missing source object.
witness.observer: The viewer, through the response error or HTTP status.
